content:
As @Jorge Luis Mayoral Perez proposed in one of our MadLean meetings, there is a 

instance : (free.{u}).PreservesMonomorphisms

for AddCommGrpCat in Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Adjunctions, and a similar one could be added for GrpCat. Trying to do that, Lean fails to infer HasZeroMorphisms GrpCat. I found zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.ZeroMorphisms, which contains this warning:

/-- A category with a zero object has zero morphisms.

It is rarely a good idea to use this. Many categories that have a zero object have zero
morphisms for some other reason, for example from additivity. Library code that uses
`zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject` will then be incompatible with these categories because
the `HasZeroMorphisms` instances will not be definitionally equal. For this reason library
code should generally ask for an instance of `HasZeroMorphisms` separately, even if it already
asks for an instance of `HasZeroObject`. -/

What is the best approach for this case? Should I just leave [HasZeroMorphisms GrpCat] as a variable? I think GrpCat doesn't have this problem because there is only one way to have zero morphisms in GrpCat. If I shouldn't use this theorem should I just prove a HasZeroMorphisms GrpCat instance locally?

Javier Gómez Zaragoza said:

I think GrpCat doesn't have this problem because there is only one way to have zero morphisms in GrpCat.

What do you mean by this? In any category whose morphisms aren't all definitionally definitional subsingletons there will always be "more than one way" to have zero morphisms.

Well, I meant something like: In GrpCat you don’t have the same problem you have in AddCommGrp since you don’t have the Preadditive HasZeroMorphisms instance, and the one derived from the HasZeroObject GrpCat is fine for this proof if I am not wrong
surely we want the zero morphisms to be defeq to 1 as a MonoidHom

I see. Since for AddCommGroup this

instance : Zero (M ⟶ N) where
  zero := ofHom 0

is in Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Preadditive, where should this

instance : Zero (M ⟶ N) where
  zero := ofHom 1

be, in something like Mathlib.Algebra.Category.MonCat.Zero? Or is there an analog of Preadditive but for monoids?
